title: Stuff
novel:
Lily and Marshall were having a fight — the biggest fight of their [[marriage|marriage]] so far. The issue? Lily wanted Marshall to get rid of some of his old [[possessions|possession]]. Specifically, his collection of [[action figures|action figure]] from every movie made before 2005.

"They're not just [[toys|toy]]," Marshall argued. "They're [[investments|investment]]. This [[Wookiee|Wookiee]] is worth more than your [[engagement|engagement]] ring!"

Wrong thing to say. Very wrong.

Lily [[stormed|storm]] out and went to Robin's apartment. "I married a [[child|child]]," she said. "He has more [[sentimental|sentiment]] [[attachment|attach]] to [[plastic|plastic]] than to me!"

Robin, who was also [[frustrated|frustrate]] with Ted for keeping every [[souvenir|souvenir]] from their [[relationship|relationship]], [[nodded|nod]] in [[sympathy|sympathy]]. "They keep things because they can't handle [[change|change]]," she said.

Meanwhile, Ted and Marshall sat in the [[apartment|apartment]] surrounded by action figures. "They don't get it," Ted said. "These aren't just things. They're [[memories|memory]]." He picked up a [[Han Solo|Han Solo]] figure. "This is from the day I met Robin."

Both couples spent the night apart, staring at the [[ceiling|ceiling]]. In the morning, Marshall showed up at Robin's door with a [[box|box]] of action figures. "I'm [[donating|donate]] these," he told Lily. "But I'm keeping three. One from the day I met you, one from the day you said yes, and one from our first kiss."

Lily [[hugged|hug]] him. "Keep four," she said. "I'm not a [[monster|monster]]."

action figure.en: a small plastic toy shaped like a film or comic character

toy.en: an object for children to play with

investment.en: something you buy hoping its value will increase

Wookiee.en: a tall hairy creature from Star Wars

storm.en: to walk somewhere quickly because you are angry

child.en: a young person; someone acting in an immature way

sentiment.en: a feeling or emotional connection to something

attachment.en: a strong feeling of love or connection to someone or something

frustrate.en: to make someone annoyed because they cannot do what they want

souvenir.en: something you keep to remember a special event or place

nod.en: to move your head up and down to show agreement

sympathy.en: the feeling of understanding another person's sadness or problems

change.en: the act of becoming different or making something different

memory.en: something you remember from the past

box.en: a container with flat sides, usually square or rectangular

donate.en: to give money or objects to help a person or organization

hug.en: to put your arms around someone to show love or comfort

monster.en: an imaginary frightening creature; a cruel person
